title: GO DOWN AND BRING AARON UP

memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text:
"The LORD replied, 'Go down and bring Aaron up with you. But the priests and the
people must not force their way through to come up to the LORD, or he will break
out against them.' So Moses went down to the people and told them."
- Ex 19:24-25 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
The chapter ends with Moses going down again and telling the people.

That is how it closes. Not with a dramatic revelation, but with a man walking
down a mountain to deliver a message. The next chapter will bring the Ten
Commandments. This one ends with obedience in motion.

Notice that Aaron is brought up with Moses. He is being drawn in, prepared for
the priestly role that is coming. God develops people gradually. Aaron does not
begin at the top of the mountain; he is brought there in stages.

And notice the repeated warning. God says it again: do not force your way
through. He has now said it three times in this chapter. Some truths need
repeating, not because God is anxious but because we are forgetful.

Here is where the chapter leaves us, and where the whole book of Hebrews picks it
up. At Sinai, the message was: stay back. Through Christ, the message became:
draw near (Heb 10:22).

The same God. The same holiness. But a way opened that did not exist at the foot
of that burning mountain.

That is the difference the cross makes.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Do you live more like someone told to stay back or invited to draw near?
2. What truth do you need to hear again because you keep forgetting it?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text:
Father, You are the God of the burning mountain, and through Jesus You have
called me near. Thank You for opening the way. Amen.
